avoid_supplements.name: Anticholinergic herbs (Jimson weed, Datura, Henbane)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Direct antagonism of neostigmine's cholinergic effects; may precipitate severe anticholinergic crisis or reduced therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Strictly contraindicate; counsel patient to avoid all anticholinergic-containing supplements

avoid_supplements.name: Muscle relaxant supplements (Valerian root in high doses)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate neuromuscular depression and reduce neostigmine efficacy in myasthenia gravis management
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative relaxation supplements with minimal neuromuscular effects

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild cholinergic stimulation may additively increase parasympathomimetic effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for excessive salivation, lacrimation, or GI effects; dose adjustment may be needed

caution_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild anticholinergic properties that could slightly reduce neostigmine efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Monitor therapeutic response and cholinergic symptoms; inform prescriber if using concurrently

avoid_foods.name: High-sodium processed foods
avoid_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium may increase fluid retention and exacerbate cholinergic side effects (bronchospasm, muscle weakness)
avoid_foods.action: Maintain moderate sodium intake; monitor for worsening respiratory or muscular symptoms

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (Broccoli, Cabbage)
caution_foods.mechanism: High vitamin K content may interact with concurrent anticoagulants if used; not direct interaction with neostigmine but relevant for poly-medicated patients
caution_foods.action: No restriction needed; consume consistently and inform prescriber of dietary vitamin K intake if on warfarin

caution_foods.name: Licorice root-containing foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May enhance fluid and sodium retention, potentially potentiating cholinergic adverse effects
caution_foods.action: Limit intake; monitor for increased GI cramping, salivation, or muscle fasciculations

monitoring_notes: Monitor closely for cholinergic crisis symptoms (muscle fasciculations, bronchospasm, bradycardia, excessive salivation) and ensure patient recognizes signs requiring immediate medical attention. Assess neuromuscular function and respiratory status regularly, particularly if supplements or dietary changes are introduced.
